requirements.text: Kindly check with the caller through written communication for the same
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM notification WHERE notification_id = 'NOTIF_031' AND incident_id = 'INC_021' AND email = 'brandon.davis@vehementcap.com' AND type = 'reminder'
assumptions: INC-000021 is incident_id INC_021 in the seed; its caller is USER_010, Brandon Davis, email brandon.davis@vehementcap.com
'written communication' read as a notification to the caller's email; send_notification is the only writing tool listed
type = reminder kept from the benchmark check; not fixed by request or policy (the incident is on hold Awaiting Caller, so a reminder fits)

id assumed next in sequence (NOTIF_031 after NOTIF_030); the only notification the task creates, so anchored by id (the seed already holds NOTIF_025, type update, to the same caller on INC_021, so a natural-key selector alone would not do)
subject, message and status not fixed by the request; not tested

requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident WHERE incident_id = 'INC_021' AND urgency = 'high' AND priority = 'high'
assumptions: priority = high from the policy matrix (section 3.1): seed impact medium x urgency high = high (seed urgency medium, priority moderate)

notes: Merged from two passes that agree on every requirement, value and disposition: no disagreements to log. Both benchmark checks are kept; the task creates one notification (NOTIF_031, the next id) to the caller of INC_021 and sets urgency high, which the policy matrix turns into priority high against the seed impact medium. Judgements both passes made the same way and the merge keeps: the incident is on hold with on_hold_reason Awaiting Caller and the request says work cannot proceed without the device, so no state change is asked and no stay is written for it (a generic invariant); no incident_sla row exists for INC_021 on the seed, so policy 6's pause rule gives nothing to test; the acting user USER_004 is a manager, whom the policy lets update incidents.
